app.description: Resource ID segment making up resource 'name'. It identifies the resource within its parent collection as described in https://google.aip.dev/122.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

display_name.description: The display name of the toolset. Must be unique within the same app.

location.description: Resource ID segment making up resource 'name'. It identifies the resource within its parent collection as described in https://google.aip.dev/122.
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

toolset_id.description:
The ID to use for the toolset, which will become the final component of
the toolset's resource name. If not provided, a unique ID will be
automatically assigned for the toolset.

mcp_toolset.description:
A toolset that contains a list of tools that are offered by the MCP
server.

mcp_toolset.custom_headers.description:
The custom headers to send in the request to the MCP server. The values
must be in the format '$context.variables.<name_of_variable>' and can be
set in the session variables. See
https://docs.cloud.google.com/customer-engagement-ai/conversational-agents/ps/tool/open-api#openapi-injection
for more details.

mcp_toolset.server_address.description:
The address of the MCP server, for example, "https://example.com/mcp/". If
the server is built with the MCP SDK, the url should be suffixed with
"/mcp/". Only Streamable HTTP transport based servers are supported. See
https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-03-26/basic/transports#streamable-http
for more details.

mcp_toolset.api_authentication.description:
Authentication information required to access tools and execute a tool
against the MCP server. For API key auth, the API key can only be sent in
the request header; sending it via query parameters is not supported.

mcp_toolset.api_authentication.api_key_c.description: Configurations for authentication with API key.

The name of the SecretManager secret version resource storing the API key.
Format: 'projects/{project}/secrets/{secret}/versions/{version}'
Note: You should grant 'roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor' role to the CES
service agent
'service-@gcp-sa-ces.iam.gserviceaccount.com'.

The parameter name or the header name of the API key.
E.g., If the API request is "https://example.com/act?X-Api-Key=", "X-Api-Key" would be the parameter name.

Key location in the request. For API key auth on MCP toolsets,
the API key can only be sent in the request header.
Possible values:
HEADER

mcp_toolset.api_authentication.bearer_to.description: Configurations for authentication with a bearer token.

mcp_toolset.api_authentication.oauth_con.description: The client ID from the OAuth provider.

The name of the SecretManager secret version resource storing the
client secret.
Format: 'projects/{project}/secrets/{secret}/versions/{version}'

Note: You should grant 'roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor' role to the CES
service agent
'service-@gcp-sa-ces.iam.gserviceaccount.com'.

OAuth grant types.
Possible values:
CLIENT_CREDENTIAL
The token endpoint in the OAuth provider to exchange for an access token.

mcp_toolset.api_authentication.service_a.description: Configurations for authentication using a custom service account.

The OAuth scopes to grant. If not specified, the default scope
'https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform' is used.

The email address of the service account used for authenticatation. CES
uses this service account to exchange an access token and the access token
is then sent in the 'Authorization' header of the request.

The service account must have the
'roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator' role granted to the
CES service agent
'service-@gcp-sa-ces.iam.gserviceaccount.com'.

Configurations for authentication with [ID
token](https://cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/token-types#id) generated
from service agent.

mcp_toolset.service_directory_config.description:
Service Directory configuration for VPC-SC, used to resolve service names
within a perimeter.

mcp_toolset.service_directory_config.ser.description:
The name of [Service
Directory](https://cloud.google.com/service-directory) service.
Format:
'projects/{project}/locations/{location}/namespaces/{namespace}/services/{service}'.
Location of the service directory must be the same as the location of the
app.

mcp_toolset.tls_config.description:
The TLS configuration. Includes the custom server certificates that the
client should trust.

mcp_toolset.tls_config.ca_certs.description:
Specifies a list of allowed custom CA certificates for HTTPS
verification.

mcp_toolset.tls_config.ca_certs.cert.description:
The allowed custom CA certificates (in DER format) for
HTTPS verification. This overrides the default SSL trust store. If this
is empty or unspecified, CES will use Google's default trust
store to verify certificates. N.B. Make sure the HTTPS server
certificates are signed with "subject alt name". For instance a
certificate can be self-signed using the following command,
openssl x509 -req -days 200 -in example.com.csr \
-signkey example.com.key \
-out example.com.crt \
-extfile <(printf "\nsubjectAltName='DNS:www.example.com'")

mcp_toolset.tls_config.ca_certs.display_.description:
The name of the allowed custom CA certificates. This
can be used to disambiguate the custom CA certificates.

open_api_toolset.description:

open_api_toolset.ignore_unknown_fields.description:

operations defined in the OpenAPI schema.

open_api_toolset.open_api_schema.description: The OpenAPI schema of the toolset.
